name: pey.llm
description: The single point of contact with a large language model provider: holds the user's connection settings in memory, speaks the OpenAI-compatible chat protocol over pey.http and interprets responses. Typed feature — the program works without AI, so a failure here must never take the whole system down; dependents deactivate with REQUIRED_DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE instead.

provides.name: pey.llm.service
provides.description: Provider-facing LLM calls. The API key lives only in this plugin's memory and in outgoing Authorization headers — never in events, errors, logs or return values; message text never appears there either. Provider error responses are mapped into categorized structured errors without leaking raw provider text. Streaming calls follow the shared flow pattern: the caller hands in text handlers and receives a handle with cancel() and a done promise that resolves exactly one of three endings — completed (the provider's end marker arrived), interrupted (with a standard structured error), or cancelled; no text is delivered after cancellation.

methods.name: setSettings
methods.description: Stores the user's connection settings in memory: base URL, model name and optional API key. Performs surface validation only (valid absolute http(s) base URL WITHOUT a query string or fragment, non-empty model name). In-flight requests keep the settings they started with.

params.name: input
params.type: { baseUrl: string, model: string, apiKey?: string } — baseUrl is the address up to (and including) the conversation path prefix, e.g. 'https://api.openai.com/v1'

methods.name: clearSettings
methods.description: Erases the stored connection settings from memory.

methods.name: getSettingsStatus
methods.description: Reports whether settings exist, the base URL and model name, and whether a key is registered. Never returns the key itself.
methods.returns: { configured: boolean, baseUrl: string | null, model: string | null, hasApiKey: boolean }

methods.name: complete
methods.description: Sends a list of messages and waits for the full response text. Returns the text with its finish reason ('stop' | 'length' | 'content_filter') and, when the provider reports it, token usage. Rejects with the structured error on failure; an error status from the provider is mapped to a categorized code.

params.name: messages
params.type: Array<{ role: 'system'|'user'|'assistant', content: Array<{ type: 'text', text: string }> }> — only text parts are accepted

params.name: options
params.type: { json?: boolean, maxTokens?: number, temperature?: number } — json asks for the provider's native JSON mode; validation of the result stays with the caller

methods.returns: Promise<{ text: string, finishReason: string, usage?: object }>

methods.name: stream
methods.description: Same conversation as complete, but the answer text is delivered progressively through handlers.onText as it arrives (SSE decoded with a streaming decoder, so a multi-byte character split across chunks stays intact). onText calls are SERIALIZED: each call happens only after the previous call's result settled (an async handler applies real backpressure; text order is preserved; done resolves only after the last delivery settled). If handlers.onText throws OR returns a rejected promise (an async handler), the transfer stops immediately, no further text is delivered, and the stream ends as { ending: 'interrupted' } with LLM_REQUEST_FAILED (including a failure on the flush-dispatched final delta); the failure never escapes as an unhandled rejection. The shared flow pattern applies: the returned handle has cancel() and a done promise resolving { ending: 'completed', finishReason, usage? } | { ending: 'interrupted', error } | { ending: 'cancelled' }. A stream that closes without the provider's end marker is interrupted, never completed.

params.name: messages
params.type: Array<{ role: 'system'|'user'|'assistant', content: Array<{ type: 'text', text: string }> }> — only text parts are accepted

params.name: options
params.type: { json?: boolean, maxTokens?: number, temperature?: number }

methods.returns: Promise<{ cancel: () => void, done: Promise<{ ending: 'completed', finishReason: string, usage?: object } | { ending: 'interrupted', error: object } | { ending: 'cancelled' }> }>

events.name: llm:settings-changed
events.description: Published when the connection settings were stored or cleared. Carries no data.
